setup: Bar end in a landmine or a padded corner
Load the free end; V-handle under the bar
Straddle the bar, feet about hip-width
Hinge to about 45°, back flat, arms long
execution: Brace, then row the handle to your belly
Drive your elbows back close to your sides
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top
Lower until your arms are straight
faults: Don't stand up taller to finish the rep
Don't jerk the weight with your hips

notes: Keep the torso angle fixed. If you have to rise up to finish the rep, the load is too heavy.
Make sure the bar end can't slip out of the landmine or corner, and protect the wall or floor with a pad.
Lift the bar into position and set it down with a flat back. Straps are fine if grip gives out first.
Smaller plates let the handle come closer to your body; large plates can stop the rep short.
The logged load is the plates added. The bar's own weight and the lever angle aren't counted, so loads aren't comparable with a barbell row or another set-up.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height. The bar's pivot end sits on the floor on the left, rising to the loaded end between the figure's feet. A V-handle hooks under the bar just behind the plates.

keyPositions.label: Hang
keyPositions.describe: Straddling the bar, hinged forward about 45° with a flat back, knees softly bent. Arms straight, hands on the V-handle under the bar, plates just off the floor.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Handle pulled to the belly, elbows driven back past the torso and close to the sides, shoulder blades squeezed. Torso angle unchanged.

ikHints: Bar pivots about its floor end; hands follow its arc
guideBrief.barPath: A short arc around the floor pivot, close to vertical under the chest
emphasise: Elbows drive back close to the body
Arms fully straight at the bottom

uncertain.note: Landmine and plate-loaded lever loads are logged as plates added, matching the landmine press. The final convention is still open (expansion research Q3). The validator may warn that added is unusual for a barbell.

FitNotes' "T-Bar Row" can mean the landmine set-up or a plate-loaded T-bar machine. Both are covered here; the chest-supported T-bar machine is a separate Should proposal and isn't an alias. "Landmine row" usually means this two-hand row; the one-arm Meadows row is separate.
